_comment: Every timing coefficient, runtime-tunable. Grounding for each is in docs/spec.md section 10. The only direct test of variable dwell against constant dwell found preference, no comprehension gain, and a speed loss - and nothing in 25 years has compared them at matched delivered rate. So every number here is a judgement, and this file is the apparatus for the experiment nobody has run.
_target_wpm: Delivered, not nominal. 300 is above the 238 wpm adult non-fiction average (Brysbaert 2019, 190 studies, 18,573 participants) and sits at the top of the band where RSVP was statistically indistinguishable from ordinary reading (Di Nocera, Ricciardi & Juola 2018: no significant difference at 250/300/350, significant loss above). Treat that as a null result from ~35 per cell, not as proof of safety - it conflicts with Acklin & Papesh, where static text beat RSVP outright. The honest framing is a PACER, not a speed multiplier: the only controlled trial of a commercial speed-reading app gained 23%, and a group merely taught to notice their own pace gained 16%.
_length_mult: Empirical target is 1.11x (gaze) to 1.36x (adjusted gaze) for an 11- vs 5-letter word. Mechanism note: the extra time is a second FIXATION, not a longer one - first-fixation duration is flat with length. Calibrate against gaze, never first-fixation. Shipped schemes range 1.04x (no-op) to 2.75x (over-corrects ~2x).
_numeric_mult: WEAK PROXY. Context-free tokens needed ~2x dwell at matched accuracy, but that is n=6 Italian readers reading random word lists ALOUD with no comprehension measure. Zero direct evidence exists on numerals under RSVP. A factor of two, not five.
_pauses: Additive, after the word. Sentence-final elevation measures +48 ms gaze and +121 ms regression-path. A boundary pause buys back a regression RSVP forbids, which is why implemented pauses look excessive against first-pass data yet defensible against total-time data.
_sentence_len_scale: Multiplies pause_sentence_ms by the word count of the sentence just ended. A boundary of paragraph IMPLIES a sentence end, so a paragraph break gets sentence pause + paragraph pause, not paragraph pause alone. Scales with working-memory load rather than punctuation mark. Spritz patent Fig. 5b - published, copied by nobody.
_word_dwell_ceiling_ms: Ceiling on the WORD component only, NEVER on the boundary pause. Above 350 ms you are inside the 200-330 ms temporal-crowding window and past the point where readers start saccading around a static word - that grounding is about how long one word hangs, not about a deliberate rest. AMENDED at Gate 2: applying it to the total flattened everything. Measured on the fixture at 250 wpm, comma/sentence/paragraph all landed at exactly 350 ms and sentence_len_scale changed 0 of 467 dwells, so the reader got the same pause at a comma as at a paragraph break. No FLOOR is set on purpose: a floor would silently ignore the user's speed setting.
_interword_gap_ms: Exposed rather than hard-coded. A blank interval after an attended item is the one manipulation shown to abolish the attentional blink - but that was letters in a detection task, so transfer to word streams is UNVERIFIED. It also unmasks stream neighbours. Two mechanisms point the same way at near-zero cost.
_resume_ramp_ms: First word after unpause. NO experimental support found anywhere. Candidate mechanisms point in opposite directions. Ship as comfort and label it as comfort.
_rewind_backoff_words: Back 5 words, then walk to the sentence start. Tapping back within the first 5 words of a sentence therefore jumps to the previous sentence. jetzt's rule, the only semantic rewind in the surveyed prior art.
_wpm_range: UI clamp. The floor is 150, not 100, for a measured reason: the word ceiling correctly forbids slowing RSVP by holding words longer (Rahman & Muter - a word left up too long re-invites the eye movements RSVP exists to remove), so below ~150 wpm all remaining budget lands in the boundary pauses. Measured on the Phase 2 fixture: longest single dwell is 1.46s at 250 wpm, 2.04s at 150, and 8.78s at 100. The 150 case is the recommended behaviour; the 100 case is not reading.
_skim_threshold_wpm: Above this the UI says Skim, not a reading rate. NOTE: RSVP at high speed is NOT a skimming tool - Masson 1983 measured it losing to ordinary skimming on the find-the-answer task, F(1,42)=19.61, with the gap WIDENING as rate rose. Real skim mode belongs on document structure, not on this slider. Detail comprehension collapses to ~53% by 500 wpm and going to 1000 costs nothing further; static text beats RSVP outright at 700 and 1000.
